items.headline: U.S. Equities Close Mixed as Tech Rebound and Apple's Woes Split Markets
items.summary: U.S. stock markets ended Tuesday with a mixed performance, as a rebound in several influential chip stocks propelled the Nasdaq and S&P 500 higher, while a significant decline in Apple ($AAPL) shares weighed on the Dow Jones Industrial Average. Investor sentiment was also shaped by easing geopolitical tensions suggesting lower energy costs, alongside lingering concerns over costly artificial intelligence (AI) investments and stretched valuations within the technology sector. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Aehr Test Systems Surges on Strong Performance
items.summary: Aehr Test Systems ($AEHR) was among the top gainers, soaring 26.17% to $64.95, indicating strong investor confidence.

items.headline: Ibotta Climbs Following Positive Momentum
items.summary: Ibotta ($IBTA) saw a substantial gain, rising 28.02% to $64.10 by mid-morning.

items.headline: Fiserv Rises After Q3 Results
items.summary: Fiserv Inc. ($FISV) was a notable gainer, advancing as much as 13.65% intra-day, following its third-quarter 2026 results where it affirmed its full-year outlook.

items.headline: Stevanato Group Plunges
items.summary: Stevanato Group S.P.A. ($STVN) experienced a significant decline, dropping 25.6% to $14.69.

items.headline: BRC Class A Falls Sharply
items.summary: BRC Class A ($BRCC) fell sharply by 23.9% to $9.64.

items.headline: Apple Shares Decline on Margin Concerns
items.summary: Apple Inc. ($AAPL) shares fell 1.83% ahead of its quarterly earnings report, with the company warning that rising memory chip prices could pressure profit margins and issuing a disappointing margin forecast.

items.headline: Shopify Nosedives on Weak Gross Merchandise Volume
items.summary: Shopify ($SHOP) nosedived 16.30% in early trading after reporting weaker-than-expected gross merchandise volume in its third quarter.

items.headline: Technology and Energy Sectors See Divergent Performance
items.summary: The technology sector demonstrated a mixed performance, with chip stocks rebounding strongly to lift the Nasdaq, while concerns over AI investment valuations continued to weigh on some larger tech names. On the other hand, the Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) declined by 4% on Monday, largely due to a sharp decline in oil prices fueled by hopes of U.S.-Iran peace talks and President Trump's announcement regarding military assistance to Israel.

items.headline: Manufacturing Index Shows Expansion, Construction Spending Falls
items.summary: The Institute for Supply Management's Manufacturing Index for October registered 55.5, an increase from September's 54.5, signaling continued expansion in manufacturing activity. However, Construction Spending for September fell by 1.9%.

items.headline: Strong Q3 GDP and High Job Openings Bolster Economic Picture
items.summary: The U.S. economy grew at an annual rate of 3.4% in the third quarter of 2026, exceeding forecasts, with cooling inflation. Additionally, September's JOLTS job openings surpassed expectations, and U.S. job quits rose to a 1-1/2-year high, reflecting a dynamic labor market.

items.headline: Major Companies Report Q3 Earnings and Guidance
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices ($AMD) announced third-quarter revenue of $13.4 billion with a 54% gross margin. Pfizer ($PFE) raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance after reporting Q3 results. Thomson Reuters ($TRI) reported a 13% increase in Q3 revenue at constant currency, driven by generative AI content licensing.

items.headline: U.S. Midterm Elections Underway, Market Watches for Implications
items.summary: The U.S. midterm elections are being held today, November 3, 2026. Historically, Wall Street tends to favor split control of Washington, viewing it as a buffer against drastic policy changes that could impact the economy.
